messages:
Alex (support): hey team — escalating an odd one from Acme: embeddings endpoint sometimes returning cache hits, sometimes misses for the same `cache_prefix`. customer is seeing extra compute (billing spike) + occasional dimension mismatch errors downstream. repro attached below. can someone take a look? :eyes:

Priya (ML Eng): thanks — can you paste the exact request bodies/headers? is this happening for batched requests only or singles too? any model/version difference?

Alex (support): quick paste: curl repro (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Cache-Prefix: user:acme:proj:42" \n  -d '{"model":"embed-lite-1536","input":["alpha","beta"]}'
```
We see: sometimes both items are hits, sometimes both misses, occasionally one hit/one miss. customer also reported one call returning a 1536-dim vector but their pipeline expects 1024 and errors on downstream reduce step. no consistent pattern by time.

Sam (runtime): that is weird. two things to check: 1) are we normalizing the `X-Cache-Prefix` header before keying? 2) are there proxies that could be injecting or duplicating headers? proxies sometimes shadow headers with different casing which bites older code.

Maya (infra): fwiw Acme sits behind a vendor reverse-proxy (AkraProxy) per their ticket. AkraProxy has a known feature that copies some headers with a `X-Forwarded-` prefix when doing internal routing. Could be duplicating `X-Cache-Prefix` as `x-cache-prefix` or `X-Cacheprefix`.

Priya (ML Eng): header casing should be irrelevant for HTTP, but our cache key builder had a bug for a short window where it used raw header keys from the request map (case-sensitive) instead of normalized header lookup. that would create two different cache keys for the same logical prefix depending on which header copy landed first. see snippet: 
```python
# old buggy code
key_parts.append(req.headers.get('X-Cache-Prefix'))
# req.headers here was an ordered dict with original case preserved
```
We fixed this in runtime v0.9.8 but tenant still on v0.9.7 could be hit.

Alex (support): interesting — Acme's traffic hit both our older and newer frontend pools during a rolling deploy last week. could explain mixed results. any quick mitigation? customer is seeing >2x token compute.

Sam (runtime): mitigation options: 1) ask Acme to set `cache_prefix` in the JSON body (we always prefer body param over headers for keying) — that'll normalize. 2) patch the 0.9.7 frontend to normalize headers at ingress (hotfix). 3) temporary route them to a pool running 0.9.8.

InfraBot: [automated] cache-miss-alert: service=embeddings env=prod pool=frontend-7 key_preview="user:acme:proj:42" miss_count=124 window=10m avg_latency=1.23s

Alex (support): also the dimension mismatch — customer saw a 1536 vector then downstream expected 1024. is that a model mismatch or something with cache?

Priya (ML Eng): two possibilities: 1) they changed the model param between calls (embed-lite-1536 vs embed-small-1024). 2) cache stored vector from one model and served it for a different model because model id wasn't included in cache key for older frontends (another bug we patched). older frontends keyed only by prefix+input hash. new key = prefix+model+version+input_hash.

Sam (runtime): putting it together: older frontend + proxy header shadowing = different prefix keyspace + missing model in key => sometimes retrieving a 1536-vector for a request expecting 1024. that matches the error symptoms.

Maya (infra): next steps I did: 1) confirmed frontend-7 is v0.9.7 and sees both `X-Cache-Prefix` and `x-cache-prefix` in raw headers for the same request. 2) added a header-normalization layer on the ingress in a temp canary (frontend-7b) that lowercases keys and forwards single canonical header. 3) routed Acme to 7b for a 30-min test window.

Alex (support): customer confirmed after routing to 7b the hit rate stabilized and billing spike stopped. they still want a root-cause summary and a fix timeline.

Priya (ML Eng): recommended permanent fixes: - backport header-normalization to all 0.9.7 frontends, - backport model-in-key fix (if not already present), - add unit test for header-casing collisions, - add a gauge/alert for cache-hit-ratio drops per-customer.

Sam (runtime): I'll open PRs: hotfix for header normalization + backport model-in-key to 0.9.7. also adding a quick CLI to scan logs for mixed-dim vectors per-customer (helps postmortem).

BillingBot: [automated] Created billing incident: INC-2026-453 — flagged duplicate compute charges for acct=acme. Pending refund review.

Alex (support): thanks everyone — I'll send Acme the summary: root cause = header shadowing by their reverse-proxy combined with older frontend behavior that didn't normalize headers or include model in cache key. mitigation = route to normalized pool or set `cache_prefix` in body. long-term = backport + tests + monitoring. marking resolved for now but leaving thread open for PR links and postmortem. :white_check_mark:
